decision: EXEC mirror carries only capture tokens (review-prefix-tree.json, luca snapshot create, When in doubt) while diff/verdict/lifecycle tokens span the three gate bodies
alternatives: pin the full token set in all four bodies
reasoning: execute.ts:412 is a cross-reference note without a gate; forcing verdict prose there would duplicate gate ground-truth against D2's collapse-to-verdict intent
risk: future editor of execute.ts reintroduces gate detail that drifts from review.ts

decision: Share the temp-index tree builder by exporting it from luca-snapshot-create.ts
alternatives: new handlers/__helpers module; duplicate the builder in the diff handler
reasoning: 2 callers within one feature = promotion tier 2; a __helpers module would be a premature promotion, duplication risks divergent snapshot semantics
risk: a third caller later forces a promotion refactor

decision: ac-15 e2e smoke invokes bun packages/luca-cli/src/cli.ts snapshot create from source instead of the linked luca binary
alternatives: call the installed luca binary; skip the e2e smoke and rely on unit tests
reasoning: source invocation is deterministic regardless of build/link state; unit tests alone would not catch citty wiring mistakes
risk: cli.ts entry may require build-time context (untested assumption) making the probe fail for harness reasons rather than wiring bugs

decision: G-CRIT-001 fixed via option (b): import.meta.main self-invoke guard in cli.ts; ac-15 keeps the source-mode probe
alternatives: build-then-probe via packages/luca/bin/luca.js; bun -e import wrapper
reasoning: guard is a 2-line idiomatic Bun change making the probe non-vacuous and build-independent; build-then-probe couples verification to build state; bun -e probes an artificial entry not the citty wiring
risk: guard could double-invoke if the built entry also calls runMain — bin/luca.js imports from dist so paths are disjoint

decision: G-ARCH-001 resolved via option (c): never-skip on the phase-execute path is an accepted, documented limitation
alternatives: persist Step 8.1 findings as parseable audits/<reviewer>.md; extend the CLI parse contract to phase-execute inline YAML
reasoning: phase-execute is the legacy path with inline-YAML findings (index.ts:967-975); ambiguous verdict fail-safes to full re-review which honors the HARD CONSTRAINT; persisting audits from the skill path has unverified stage-gate legality and extending the parse contract doubles the CLI cite grammar for a legacy surface
risk: phase-execute users never benefit from the skip optimization; if the legacy path outlives expectations the limitation may warrant follow-up option (a)

decision: Placed luca snapshot test with a --json flags variant near luca verification tests; sibling flag-variant tests exist so added one
reasoning: Plan specified exact Set entries and expected categories; only test placement/flag-variant was inferred from file conventions
risk: None significant; snapshot verbs intentionally fall to luca-write per plan

decision: Handler is phase-agnostic (no allowedPhases) and errors when no phase is active; exported REVIEW_PREFIX_TREE_RELPATH constant alongside the tree-builder
alternatives: Write payload without a phase key when state has no active phase
Hardcode the payload path separately in both handlers
reasoning: Plan requires capture to be legal in both EXECUTING and REVIEWING; sibling phase-agnostic tools omit allowedPhases. The payload requires a phase slug for the diff handler's mismatch check, so no-active-phase must be an error. A shared exported constant prevents path-spelling drift in the Wave-2 diff handler.
risk: If a future flow needs snapshots outside an active phase, the handler will refuse
reviewHint: Confirm no-allowedPhases + error-on-inactive-phase matches the diff-handler expectations in Task 1.2.1

decision: Cite parser is strict fail-safe: an unknown severity tag (e.g. [BLOCKER]) or a 'File:' line appearing before any finding bullet is a parse FAILURE mapping to verdict ambiguous, and NOTE-finding File lines are silently skipped.
alternatives: Lenient parser: ignore unknown severity tags and orphan File: lines, collecting only well-formed MUST-FIX/SHOULD-FIX cites
Regex-scan the whole file for any 'File: path:line' regardless of finding severity (over-collects NOTE cites, weakening zero-overlap proofs)
reasoning: The task mandates 'any parse failure -> ambiguous' but does not enumerate what counts as a failure. Strictness is the fail-safe direction: a malformed audit degrades to a re-review (ambiguous), never to a vacuous skip. Skipping NOTE File lines matches the reviewer output format, which defines File cites only under MUST-FIX/SHOULD-FIX.
risk: Audits with benign prose containing a leading 'File:' line or nonstandard severity tags will force ambiguous verdicts more often than strictly necessary, costing extra re-reviews (cost, not correctness).
reviewHint: Check parseAuditCitePaths strictness against real audit files produced by the reviewer subagents.

decision: Did not add 'snapshot create'/'snapshot diff' entries to WRITE_COMMAND_PHASES (luca-core step-artifacts.ts) — absence skips the phase self-check, matching the handlers' phase-agnostic design
reasoning: Task scope listed exactly three luca-cli changes and forbade edits beyond registration; runtime behavior is identical either way since runWriteHandler skips the check when the key is absent
risk: A future registry-completeness check could flag the missing entries; a reviewer may want explicit [] entries added in luca-core
reviewHint: Consider adding explicit phase-agnostic [] entries for snapshot create/diff to WRITE_COMMAND_PHASES in a follow-up

decision: MF4 uncited-actionable detection implemented at bullet granularity (each MUST-FIX/SHOULD-FIX bullet must have >=1 File: cite before next bullet/EOF), not markdown-section granularity
alternatives: require exactly one cite per bullet
reasoning: reviewer.ts output format is bullet-based (- [SEVERITY]), not heading-based; bullet granularity is stricter and matches the parser's existing mode machine; prose headings like '## MUST-FIX' with 'None.' bodies contain no bullets so they still parse (covered by test)
risk: an audit format using headings-only findings without bullets would not be caught, but that format also produces no cites so the empty-cite-set ambiguous fail-safe still fires

decision: Embedded-separator cites rejected by tightening the CITE regex to ^([^:\s]+):(\d+)$ (auditor-blessed option) rather than post-extraction string checks; crash-after-consumption guard implemented by extracting the pipeline into computeDiffVerdict() wrapped in try/catch
alternatives: post-extraction includes(':')/whitespace check on the greedy match
resolve each cite via git cat-file -e against prior/current trees
reasoning: regex tightening makes the garbage forms fail at the same parse-failure choke point with the existing unparsable-cite error path; cat-file resolution was the auditor's stretch option but heavier and not required to close the named routes; function extraction avoids re-indenting 160 handler lines and keeps the handler slim
risk: a real repo path containing a colon or space would now fail cite parsing and force a full re-review — fail-safe by design, cost is only re-review
